## 2. How long each structure survives

### Which single flips a structure can survive

Every cell within two of the structure is flipped once, on its own, and the board is run for 96 generations to see whether the structure comes back. If a structure died when a flip landed in a fraction f of that neighbourhood, and nothing else mattered, its lifetime under noise would be about 1 / (p f A).

| structure | cells | neighbourhood | fatal flips | fatal fraction | predicted lifetime at p = 1e-3 | measured |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| block | 4 | 36 | 28 | 78% | 36 | 44 |
| beehive | 6 | 52 | 38 | 73% | 26 | 32 |
| loaf | 7 | 58 | 43 | 74% | 23 | 28 |
| boat | 5 | 46 | 33 | 72% | 30 | 39 |
| tub | 4 | 45 | 25 | 56% | 40 | 45 |
| pond | 8 | 60 | 52 | 87% | 19 | 23 |
| blinker | 3 | 35 | 25 | 71% | 40 | 47 |
| toad | 6 | 46 | 34 | 74% | 29 | 30 |
| beacon | 8 | 56 | 50 | 89% | 20 | 24 |
| glider | 5 | 46 | 33 | 72% | 30 | 31 |
| lightweight spaceship | 9 | 70 | 52 | 74% | 19 | 25 |

## 3. One flip on a settled board

A Conway soup is run to a cycle, one cell is flipped, and the flipped board is compared with the untouched one for 400 generations.

| outcome after 400 generations | trials |
| --- | --- |
| healed | 52 of 60 |
| persistent | 8 of 60 |

Mean largest difference: 11.6 cells over all trials, 80.6 cells over the trials where the damage did not heal.


## 4. Damage spreading under noise

Two boards that differ in one cell are driven by identical noise for 400 generations after a 600-generation burn-in, on a 64x64 torus, 20 trials per point. Because the noise is shared, any difference left at the end came from the single flip.

| flip probability | trials where the damage healed completely | mean final difference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 15 of 20 | 1.74% of the board |
| 3e-5 | 17 of 20 | 1.27% of the board |
| 1e-4 | 14 of 20 | 3.09% of the board |
| 3e-4 | 13 of 20 | 4.48% of the board |
| 1e-3 | 14 of 20 | 4.48% of the board |
| 3e-3 | 16 of 20 | 2.66% of the board |
| 1e-2 | 8 of 20 | 13.88% of the board |
| 3e-2 | 4 of 20 | 31.03% of the board |
